The BANcode Registry

Four diagnostic blocks in the System Control Plane.

Block Range Severity Behavior
BANcode (B+) 0x0011A000–0x0011A7FF hard halt or roll back the stream
WARNcode (W+) 0x0011A800–0x0011ABFF soft warn and continue
COMcode (C+) 0x0011AC00–0x0011ADFF informational communication and datagrams
SOFTcode (S+) 0x0011AE00–0x0011AEFF runtime soft-fault handling

Registry slots are assigned in sudat/assignments.txt. In 0.1.0 all slots are unassigned, pending the 0.2.0 registry work; the blocks themselves are frozen and named.

System and App modes

The registry runs in one of two operating modes. Both modes share the identical codepoint registry — BANcode, WARNcode, COMcode and SOFTcode occupy the same blocks and carry the same meaning. The mode only controls how a fatal BANcode (B+) is handled when it is dispatched:

Mode Fatal B+ handling
System mode (default) Dispatches through the Kernel Security Traps (0x7FFFFFF0–0x7FFFFFFE). Each of the 15 trap slots governs a cluster of 128 B+ BANcodes; the kernel’s damage-control handler for the cluster runs. This is the krnl dispatch path.
App mode Bypasses kernel dispatch entirely. A fatal B+ BANcode crashes the application through a registered App-level crash handler, keeping the kernel trap machinery reserved for the kernel.

The mode is selected at runtime (bancode_set_mode(), bancode_get_mode()) and defaults to System unless an app-mode build is requested at compile time (BANCODE_DEFAULT_MODE). App handlers are registered with bancode_register_app_crash_handler().

System mode is for krnl: fatal BANcodes route to Kernel Security Traps. App mode is for application code: fatal BANcodes crash the app via its own handler — never touching the krnl trap table.

See also the System Control Plane and traps.
